narratives.Overview:
## What happened

Two frozen tests/specs reject implementations that follow the surrounding fixture style.

### Lab 9 — greeting CLI vs unit test

`src/cli.mjs` is `console.log(greeting(process.argv[2]));`.

With no argument, Node passes `undefined` (arity 1). The unit test uses `greeting()` (arity 0) for the teammate fallback.

A learner who writes `if (arguments.length > 0 && typeof name !== "string") throw ...` passes the test and fails the helper’s fallback CLI check.

The task text says “missing or blank” but does not say the CLI always passes `argv[2]`.

### Capstone — `/nonempty title/` vs fixture phrasing

Starter `validateItems` throws `work-item title must be nonempty`.

The frozen test is:

```js
assert.throws(() => addWorkItem([], "   "), /nonempty title/);
```

`"work-item title must be nonempty"` does **not** contain the substring `"nonempty title"` (the words are reversed: “title … nonempty”).

On Node 24.20.0, `/nonempty title/.test("work-item title must be nonempty") === false`.

After red, the test is frozen. Learners who copy the fixture’s own error phrasing cannot go green. The passing message is something like `nonempty title is required`.

The duplicate-title finding *does* specify an exact phrase. The blank-title case does not.

## Suggested repair

- Lab 9: document that the CLI passes `process.argv[2]`, which may be `undefined`, or call `greeting` only when the arg is present.
- Capstone: change the regex to `/nonempty/` or `/title must be nonempty/`, or state the required message before red.
